entities.summary: Zhao Rukuo, also romanised as Zhao Rugua, Chau Ju-kua, or as Zhao Rushi, was a Chinese government official and writer during the Song dynasty. He wrote a two-volume book titled Zhu Fan Zhi. The book deals with the world known to the Chinese in the twelfth and thirteenth centuries; the first volume is a list of foreign places with descriptions of each place and the customs of its local people. The second volume is a catalog of trade goods. Zhao Rukuo was a journalists & chroniclers from Tiantai (1170-04-19, Tiantai–1231-08-18). Holds notable historical significance, documented across 0 language editions of Wikipedia. Relevant to cause-and-effect analysis.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Zhao Rukuo's book Zhu Fan Zhi provides a unique window into the global knowledge of the Chinese during the 12th and 13th centuries, detailing trade goods and customs from over 60 countries. This information has been crucial for understanding the early history of international trade.
